That is an absence, recorded as one -- it is not evidence that they were the archive's own.  THE 22 CARPET PLATES UNDER carpet/ ARE DERIVED FROM ELEVEN ILLUMINATIONS THE OWNER UPLOADED ON 26 AUGUST 2026 (C433). Their hand and licence are recorded exactly as C435 ruled — his, through a tool, on his own standing authorisation, resting on his word. NO MODEL IS NAMED because none was named to the archive. Each row states the crop, the rotation and the recolour that made it, because 'derived, not copied' is a claim and this archive does not publish a claim it cannot measure; the recipe is map/carpet_pages.json and the tool is map/gen_carpet_plates.py.

assets.licence: published at the owner's explicit direction, 31 July 2026 — his words: the map lines, my request rules. This is NOT a grant from the rightsholder and is not recorded as one. The archive states whose hand it is and on whose instruction it is published, which is the true thing it can say. See CLAUDE.md, The Baynes sheet.

assets.what: a 304-glyph subset of Unifont CSUR covering the ConScript Unicode Registry blocks for Tengwar (U+E000-E07F, 128/128), Cirth (U+E080-E0FF, 128/128) and Sarati (U+E390-E3BF, 48/48)
assets.hand: Roman Czyborra, Paul Hardy, Qianqian Fang, Andrew Miller, Johnnie Weaver and the Unifont contributors; subset and renamed for this archive
assets.licence: OFL-1.1 and GPL-2.0-or-later with the GNU Font Embedding Exception (dual)
assets.licence_read_from: the font's own name table, ID 13, verified after subsetting; the full text ships beside it as fonts/ArdaCSUR-LICENSE.txt
assets.source: https://unifoundry.com/unifont/
assets.renamed: RENAMED from 'Unifont CSUR' to 'Arda CSUR' because it is a MODIFIED version. The OFL requires that of derivatives, and it also stops a reader mistaking a 304-glyph subset for the 11,691-glyph original.
assets.why_it_matters: the archive had NO Cirth and NO Sarati font. This is the only freely-licensed source of either that could be verified, and its licence was read from the file rather than taken from a third party.

assets.licence: OFL-1.1
assets.source: https://at.boktypografen.se/downloads.htm (eldamar1_1.zip)

assets.what: Tengwar Telcontar 0.09 — 424 glyphs, 112 in the ConScript tengwar block, 49 in the Cirth block, 0 Sarati
assets.hand: Johan Winge (2005-2010) and J. 'Mach' Wust (2009-2010)
assets.licence: GNU General Public License — BARE GPL, with NO font exception
assets.licence_read_from: the font's own name table, ID 13 and 14; second witness the AUR PKGBUILD declaring GPL3. Full notice ships beside it as fonts/TengwarTelcontar-LICENCE.txt
assets.source: the Free Tengwar Font Project; this copy taken from a mirrored page rather than from SourceForge, whose release ZIPs sit behind a Cloudflare interstitial
assets.ruled: the owner ruled 12 August 2026 that it MAY BE SERVED. Recorded, not re-litigated.
assets.note: the absence of a font exception is unusual and is stated in the licence file rather than smoothed over: a sibling font in the same mirror spells one out in full. GPL compliance asks that the notice travel with the font, the licence be named and linked, and the source remain obtainable upstream.

assets.what: A passage of continuous sarati in vertical columns, the Two Trees. Its reading, supplied by the archive's owner: Valar empannen Aldaru / mi kon-alkorin / ar sealalan taro / ar silankalan ve laure ve misil — the Gods planted the Two Trees in a blessed garth, and they grow high and shine like gold like silver. The forms are attested early Qenya; their weight sits in Vinyar Tengwar 27, which this archive holds only as a machine reading, so the text is attested and uncitable at once.

assets.what: The light initial, 34x34 units: a field of red-lead dots outlining an empty letter slot, and nothing else. The most authentic of the three. EADFRITH'S DOT-OUTLINING, the Lindisfarne signature -- letterforms surrounded by a stipple of red lead (minium). 10,600 dots are counted on the Luke incipit alone, f.139r; replication at about thirty dots a minute puts that one page's stippling at six hours of continuous work. Modern conservation microscopy finds craquelure in the dots themselves, so they were raised mounds of pigment rather than flat specks.

GERMANIC, by descent -- Salin's Style II, the Migration-period animal art of Sutton Hoo, Taplow and the Staffordshire Hoard: ribbon-bodied, snake-headed, deliberately non-naturalistic, gripping with its jaws to resolve a strand-end. The popular account has this backwards and the archive should not repeat it: THE SPIRALS ARE CELTIC AND THE BEASTS ARE GERMANIC.
